review.title: Reads fail when Redis Cache is down
review.detail: Every read from API Servers goes through Redis Cache; misses continue to the data store, but if the cache itself is unavailable reads have no other path.
review.suggestion: Let reads degrade to the data store when the cache errors (with a circuit breaker so the store is not flooded), or run the cache with replicas.

review.title: Redis Cache waits indefinitely on PostgreSQL
review.detail: No timeout on PostgreSQL: a slow or hung dependency keeps Redis Cache's workers waiting until its pool fills and requests queue behind them.
review.suggestion: Set per-call timeouts a little above each dependency's p99 (for example 2× p99), keeping their sum inside the caller's own budget.

review.title: PostgreSQL has no replica
review.detail: A primary failure is an outage for every read and write that reaches it.
review.suggestion: Add a standby or read replicas (relational), a replica set (document stores) or replication factor 3 (wide-column).

review.title: No rate limit at the edge
review.detail: Nothing in front of the system caps traffic, so a spike, a retry storm or a bot flood reaches every tier at full force.
review.suggestion: Add a rate limit on the gateway or load balancer sized to the capacity you have measured.

review.title: Load Balancer waits indefinitely on API Servers
review.detail: No timeout on API Servers: a slow or hung dependency keeps Load Balancer's workers waiting until its pool fills and requests queue behind them.
review.suggestion: Set per-call timeouts a little above each dependency's p99 (for example 2× p99), keeping their sum inside the caller's own budget.

review.title: PostgreSQL has fewer connections than callers
review.detail: Up to 8 blocking workers (API Servers) can wait on PostgreSQL, which accepts 6 connections. When it slows down, 2 requests queue for a connection and fail after 1,000 ms.
review.suggestion: Size application pools to the database's real concurrency, add a pooler, or cap service concurrency.

review.title: Load Balancer is a single instance
review.detail: Load Balancer is modelled as one self-hosted instance; if it stops, nothing behind it is reachable.
review.suggestion: Run two instances with failover (floating IP, DNS) or use a managed load balancer.

reviewRules.edge-rate-limit: No rate limit at the edge
